v0.2.0: Jev as a coding agent's memory manager

The first release. Jev decides what a coding agent keeps in its context. It can score text but never write it, so everything the agent sees is original, and anything moved out comes back byte for byte.

![python demo.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Waxmell114514/jev-compaction/v0.2.0/docs/demo.gif)

## What's in it

- **Admission with a profile.** One Jev request per tool output asks each segment: keep it? what type is it? what role does it play (code to change, evidence, navigation, noise)? how long will it matter? is it a prompt injection? Low-value runs become one-line pointers that say what they hide; injections are quarantined.
- **`expand` and `recall`.** `expand` returns the text behind a pointer byte for byte. `recall` finds earlier output from a loose description: a profile filter, a lexical shortlist, then a Jev rerank.
- **Supersession.** From tool-call arguments alone, it tracks which outputs a later call made obsolete: the same command rerun, the same lines re-read, or the file edited since.
- **The work area.** Before each request, outputs in the transcript's tail that have served their purpose become pointers, but only when `dropped × turns left × cache price` beats the cost of breaking the prompt cache.
- **Calibration.** Every decision is logged, and thresholds per tool are fitted from what the agent later used.
- **Integrations.** An [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) plugin, an HTTP sidecar for any other harness, and a complete OpenAI-compatible agent loop (`run_agent.py`).
- **Jev on OpenRouter** (#1). Set `JEV_BASE_URL=https://openrouter.ai/api/alpha` and `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`. `JEV_API_KEY`, `JEV_MODEL` and `JEV_PATH` cover any other endpoint.

## Results on SWE-bench Verified (OpenCode)

- About a quarter of tool output was removed at admission, and the resolve rate was unchanged (20/23 vs 20/23).
- Gating on *role* halved how often code the agent later edited had been elided (11 records vs 21).
- Injection: 17 of 18 planted instructions were caught, with no false positives in 2,499 real segments.
- `recall`: the target was in the top 3 for 80% of queries (49% for BM25), and 69% for queries with no identifiers (18% for BM25).
- The work area: requests were about 16% smaller, and about 10% cheaper on comparable runs at a $3 / $0.30 price sheet.

These runs used a free model with one run per arm, so differences of a few points are noise. [RESULTS.md](https://github.com/Waxmell114514/jev-compaction/blob/v0.2.0/RESULTS.md) has the setup, the intervals and the caveats.

## Try it

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Waxmell114514/jev-compaction && cd jev-compaction
uv venv .venv && uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python -e '.[dev]'
.venv/bin/python demo.py          # offline, no key needed
```

The page: https://waxmell114514.github.io/jev-compaction/
